purpose: 366-item classification pass on the 'junk drawer' catalog items (things sitting under Miscellaneous/Other in the source data with no real bucket) - proposes a real destination bucket for each item instead of leaving them all lumped as Misc.
why_relocated_here: Originally dropped in inbox/, ended up stuck in _needs_review/ because the file's top level is a JSON array and the inbox watcher's classifier requires a JSON object at the top level - a format mismatch, not a data problem. Moved directly into data-layer/derived/ (C3's authorized path) rather than reshaping it to satisfy the watcher, since this is derived analysis output, not a doc/handoff for the watcher to route.

fields.name: item name as it appears in the source catalog
fields.uuid: source UUID if the catalog had one; often blank for junk-drawer items
fields.current_section: the section the item currently sits under (almost all Miscellaneous/Other)
fields.current_category: the category the item currently sits under
fields.proposed_bucket: this pass's proposed destination bucket; UNCLASSIFIED means no confident call was made
fields.proposed_destination: free-text explanation of the proposed move, including SPLIT cases where an item may belong in two places (e.g. commodity-matched items should go to Commodities, decorative duplicates stay as collectibles)
fields.commodity_name_match_204endpoint: true if the item's name matches an entry in the 204-endpoint commodity name list, meaning it may actually be a sellable commodity rather than a collectible

open_items_for_sleven: 28 UNCLASSIFIED items and all SPLIT-flagged proposed_destination entries still need a human call on final bucket placement - this file proposes, it doesn't decide. Ties into the standing open item-taxonomy ruling in CURRENT-STATE.md.

companion_files.junk-drawer-366-classified.json: the 366 classified items, array of objects, fields as above.
